newsitem.title: USA: Dollar begins weaker in US then edges up post-data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar begins weaker in US then edges up post-data.

text.p: The dollar began weaker after fresh signs of U.S./Japan trade tensions emerged in overseas dealings, but crept marginally higher after morning U.S. data showed firm second quarter growth and highlighted strength in the labor market.
Despite modest morning gains, dealers said the dollar appeared to be in an end-of-the-month consolidation mode and predicted pressure even in the face of bullish fundamentals.
"The consensus view is that the dollar is consolidating and most traders are looking for a move lower," said Jeremy Fand, foreign exchange strategist at Bank of Boston.
The dollar opened weaker at 1.8315/25 marks against 1.8360/70 at Wednesday's close. It began at 118.15/25 yen versus 118.40/45.

Fand suggested that the market was more interested in third quarter manufacturing and payrolls data, due Friday, than Thursday's second quarter growth figures which confirmed what most economists had expected.
The Commerce Department reported that the U.S. economy expanded at a 2.2 percent pace in the April-June period of this year, slightly above expectations for a 1.9 percent advance.
However, first quarter growth was revised down substantially to 4.9 percent from its originally reported breakneck pace of 5.9 percent.
A report from the Labor Department, which was released simultaneously, showed a marked fall in jobless claims from 299,000 to 277,000 in the July 26 week -- its lowest level since January of 1974.

The dollar began the day under pressure after sinking to a low of 117.48 yen overseas. Remarks from Takao Tominaga, the vice chairman of Japan's Automobile Manufacturers' Association, weighed on the rate, dealer said.
Tominaga pegged the appropriate range for dollar/yen at 110 to 120, and said he did not want the rate to strengthen from its current levels due to its implications for trade.

His remarks came on the heels of comments from U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky, who said earlier this week that Japan had not gone far enough in opening up its auto market to outside competition.
"Quite clearly there are worries about dollar/yen rallying above 120 both from the Japanese and U.S. authorities," said Bob Savage, chief dealer at Lehman Brothers.
With fundamentals and interest rate differentials still pointing in dollar/yen's favor, Savage said the rate was being pulled in two directions.
On Thursday, Japan reported that housing starts fell 11.6 percent and construction orders slumped by 6.5 percent in June versus the prior year.
"The data continue to be extraordinarily weak ... and the JGB market is close to its all time high which is hard to understand in a country which has an economy that's growing," said Savage.

A big mover on Thursday was sterling, which benefitted early from comments by British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown. Brown said in an interview in Wednesday's Times newspaper that he had no plans for a special autumn budget to attempt to put the brakes on consumer spending.

Traders said the Bank of England would probably be forced take it upon themselves to dampen spending by raising rates. Until rates begin to cut into growth, however, sterling should remain strong and the export sector should remain under severe pressure, they predicted.
In mid-morning trade, sterling stood above 3.0 marks and remained well-bid against the dollar. It opened at $1.6398/08 against $1.6280/90 on Wednesday.
Dealers said dollar strength against the mark depended on the rate's ability to fight off profit-takers and hold above support in the mid-1.82 area.
"As long as the dollar is above 1.8250 the uptrend is still intact," said Hans Boman, chief spot dealer at Swedbank in New York. "If we break that we could see a bigger correction on the downside."

In other trade on Thursday, the dollar opened at 1.5090/00 Swiss francs versus 1.5120/30 at Wednesday's close, and debuted lower at Canadian $1.3804/09 against C$1.3810/20. The Australian dollar began at $0.7432/37, slightly down from $0.7442/47.
(( -- Noah Barkin, N.A. Forex Unit, 212-859-1673 ))
